newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Samsung said to hold final talks on Fokker takeover.
newsitem.headline: Samsung said to hold final talks on Fokker takeover.

text.p: Dutch news media said on Tuesday that a high-level South Korean delegation was in Amsterdam to finalise a takeover of failed aircraft-maker Fokker NV.

But receivers handling Fokker's affairs declined to comment on the reports that two senior officials of Samsung Aerospace Industries had come to set the seal on a takeover of Fokker which was declared bankrupt earlier this year.

A spokeswoman for the receivers said they had nothing to add to a brief statement issued on September 13 in which they said Samsung Aerospace had been given the exclusive right to examine Fokker's books with a view to a possible takeover bid.

Dutch news agency ANP and several newspapers named the Samsung Aerospace executives as Yu Moo-sung and Lee Dae-won, adding that they had dined with the Fokker receivers at a luxury hotel in Amsterdam on Monday and would hold further talks today.
Samsung Aerospace's press office in Seoul declined to comment on the Dutch reports but said the two executives had been visiting neighbouring Germany on business.
Fokker was declared bankrupt in March after majority shareholder Daimler Benz Aerospace said it was no longer able to bear the Dutch company's huge losses.
Since then Samsung Aerospace has emerged as the only serious candidate to take over Fokker's core plane-making business which has maintained a low level of production since the bankruptcy.

De Volkskrant newspaper quoted Dutch engineering firm Stork NV's chairman Jan Hovers as saying there were plans for Samsung to acquire a 70 percent stake in a relaunched Fokker, with Stork and the Dutch state each taking 15 percent.
In July Stork acquired the profitable Fokker Aviation maintenance business which remained outside the bankruptcy.
Hovers warned that it was too early yet to assume that Samsung would emerge as Fokker's saviour.
"I would like to put the optimism a little into perspective. There are various plans but the question is how realistic they are," he told De Volkskrant.
Samsung Aerospace is seeking to establish itself as a serious player in the world aerospace industry but dropped out of a joint Asian aircraft project in June.
ANP said that if Samsung did go ahead with a takeover of Fokker it would transfer some production to South Korea.
